notes:
Summary: early evaluation for enterprise code search + RAG platform. Primary pain: extremely large embedding corpus (30-120M vectors across mono-repo + historical artifacts), frequent re-indexing (nightly + hot updates on commit), and strict SSO/SAML + data residency. Target metrics: p95 retrieval+rerkank <= 250ms for web UX, average cost per query target <$0.02 (includes ANN lookup + top-k cross-encoder rerank). Team wants clear tradeoffs: indexing speed vs unit cost; how caching and incremental re-embed pipelines affect unit economics.

Key quotes: "Our devs expect search to be as fast as local grep for common queries — 200ms feels like the bar." — Head of Platform.

Architecture preferences stated on call: prefer hybrid approach: vector index (ANN) for recall + lightweight cross-encoder reranker for top-10; fallback to smaller LLM for summarization. Strong preference for private deployment or VPC with customer-managed KMS.

Technical constraints / specifics:
- Corpus: ~85M repo file chunks, pre-tokenized and fingerprinted. Many very short vectors (code snippets 16-128 tokens).
- Reindex cadence: nightly full pass plus real-time upserts for new commits (expect 5000 upserts/day).
- Desired throughput: 250-400 QPS peak during working hours; baseline 40-60 QPS.
- Latency SLO: 95th <= 250ms end-to-end for top-k retrieval+rerank when reranker is lightweight ONNX quantized; 99th < 500ms acceptable if degraded to fallback.
- Cost sensitivity: procurement asks for cost modeling at 50M, 100M index scale. Goal: <$0.02/query at 100M with reranking and summarization on 10% of queries.
- Models: prefer open models. Interested in quantized 13B for generation, smaller cross-encoder (sentence-transformer-style or tiny cross-encoder) for rerank to keep latency down.
- Storage: vector index hot tier (NVMe) + cold tier for older artifacts.
- Security: SSO + SCIM, org-scoped audit logs, retention controls, per-route token & telemetry, client-side encryption for at-rest vectors.

Recent conversation snippets:
- 2026-01-27 call: demo of current search; we discussed incremental upsert model and how Redwood handles prefix caching/kv cache across identical queries. They asked about model pinning and deterministic rerank results for offline QA.
- 2026-02-12 SSO demo with infra: IdP is Okta; asked about SCIM provisioning speed and cert rotation cadence.

POC ask: Redwood to run 1-week POC on Dedicated pool with a 50M subset (random but repo-representative) to measure: index build time, daily incremental upsert latency, p50/p95 query latency with top-10 rerank, and cost per logical query. POC deliverable should include SLO breach cases and cost sensitivity scenarios.

Decision factors for Auric:
- Does Redwood provide deterministic rerank results given model/version pinning + seed management?
- Is there a recommended shard/partition size and compaction schedule for 50-120M vectors?
- How does Redwood's caching/batching reduce per-token costs for code-length short sequences?
- Security/compliance: full SOC2 + on-prem option preferred; will escalate to procurement once SSO and data residency clauses are in place.

Sales notes / next actions:
- AE: send tailored POC SOW and pricing matrix for Dedicated vs Private (include burst & autoscale scenarios).
- SE: propose index shard plan and incremental re-embed pipeline (lambda / batch design), include sample benchmarks on 25M/50M/100M.
- CSM: prepare onboarding checklist for Okta SSO + SCIM endpoints.

Misc refs: jira RWINF-3217 includes early latency failures on cross-encoder re-rank in staging; see drive doc for raw latency traces.
